## Scope of this Part and interpretation

## 62.1

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (1) This Part contains rules about arbitration claims. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (2) In this Part –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (a) ‘the 1950 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1950 1 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (b) ‘the 1975 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1975 2 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (c) ‘the 1979 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1979 3 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (d) ‘the 1996 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1996 4 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (e) references to –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (i) the 1996 Act; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (ii) any particular section of that Act

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] include references to that Act or to the particular section of that Act as applied with modifications by the ACAS Arbitration Scheme (England and Wales) Order 2001 5 ; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (f) ‘arbitration claim form’ means a claim form in the form set out in Practice Direction 62. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.1] (3) Part 58 (Commercial Court) applies to arbitration claims in the Commercial Court, Part 59 (Circuit Commercial Court) applies to arbitration claims in the Circuit Commercial Court and Part 60 (Technology and Construction Court claims) applies to arbitration claims in the Technology and Construction Court, except where this Part provides otherwise. ## I CLAIMS UNDER THE 1996 ACT

## Interpretation

## 62.2

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (1) In this Section of this Part ‘arbitration claim’ means –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (a) any application to the court under the 1996 Act;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (b) a claim to determine –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (i) whether there is a valid arbitration agreement;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (ii) whether an arbitration tribunal is properly constituted; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] what matters have been submitted to arbitration in accordance with an arbitration agreement;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (c) a claim to declare that an award by an arbitral tribunal is not binding on a party; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (d) any other application affecting –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (i) arbitration proceedings (whether started or not); or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (ii) an arbitration agreement. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.2] (2) This Section of this Part does not apply to an arbitration claim to which Sections II or III of this Part apply. ## Starting the claim

## 62.3

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.3] (1) Except where paragraph (2) applies an arbitration claim must be started by the issue of an arbitration claim form in accordance with the Part 8 procedure. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.3] (2) An application under section 9 of the 1996 Act to stay legal proceedings must be made by application notice to the court dealing with those proceedings. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.3] (3) The courts in which an arbitration claim may be started are set out in Practice Direction 62. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.3] (4) Rule 30.5 applies with the modification that a judge of the Technology and Construction Court may transfer the claim to any other court or specialist list. ## Arbitration claim form

## 62.4

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (1) An arbitration claim form must –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (a) include a concise statement of –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (i) the remedy claimed; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (ii) any questions on which the claimant seeks the decision of the court;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (b) give details of any arbitration award challenged by the claimant, identifying which part or parts of the award are challenged and specifying the grounds for the challenge;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (c) show that any statutory requirements have been met;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (d) specify under which section of the 1996 Act the claim is made;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (e) identify against which (if any) defendants a costs order is sought; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (f) specify either –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (i) the persons on whom the arbitration claim form is to be served, stating their role in the arbitration and whether they are defendants; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (ii) that the claim is made without notice under section 44(3) of the 1996 Act and the grounds relied on. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (2) Unless the court orders otherwise an arbitration claim form must be served on the defendant within 1 month from the date of issue and rules 7.5 and 7.6 are modified accordingly. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.4] (3) Where the claimant applies for an order under section 12 of the 1996 Act (extension of time for beginning arbitral proceedings or other dispute resolution procedures), he may include in his arbitration claim form an alternative application for a declaration that such an order is not needed. ## Service out of the jurisdiction

## 62.5

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (1) Subject to paragraph (2A), the court may give permission to serve an arbitration claim form out of the jurisdiction if –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (a) the claimant seeks to –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (i) challenge; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (ii) appeal on a question of law arising out of,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] an arbitration award made within the jurisdiction;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (The place where an award is treated as made is determined by section 53 of the 1996 Act.)

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (b) the claim is for an order under section 44 of the 1996 Act; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (c) the claimant –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (i) seeks some other remedy or requires a question to be decided by the court affecting an arbitration (whether started or not), an arbitration agreement or an arbitration award; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (ii) the seat of the arbitration is or will be within the jurisdiction or the conditions in section 2(4) of the 1996 Act are satisfied. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (2) An application for permission under paragraph (1) must be supported by written evidence –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (a) stating the grounds on which the application is made; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (b) showing in what place or country the person to be served is, or probably may be found. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] 2A) An arbitration claim form falling within (1)(a) to (c) above may be served out of the jurisdiction without permission if—

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (a)the seat of the arbitration is or will be in England and Wales; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (b)the respondent is party to the arbitration agreement in question. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (3) Rules 6.34, 6.35 and 6.40 to 6.46 apply to the service of an arbitration claim form under paragraph (1) or (2A). [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.5] (4) An order giving permission to serve an arbitration claim form out of the jurisdiction must specify the period within which the defendant may file an acknowledgment of service. ## Notice

## 62.6

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.6] (1) Where an arbitration claim is made under section 24, 28 or 56 of the 1996 Act, each arbitrator must be a defendant. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.6] (2) Where notice must be given to an arbitrator or any other person it may be given by sending him a copy of –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.6] (a) the arbitration claim form; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.6] (b) any written evidence in support. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.6] (3) Where the 1996 Act requires an application to the court to be made on notice to any other party to the arbitration, that notice must be given by making that party a defendant. ## Case management

## 62.7

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.7] (1) Part 26 and any other rule that requires a party to file a directions questionnaire does not apply. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.7] (2) Arbitration claims are allocated to the multi-track. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.7] (3) Part 29 does not apply. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.7] (4) The automatic directions set out in Practice Direction 62 apply unless the court orders otherwise. ## Stay of legal proceedings

## 62.8

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (1) An application notice seeking a stay of legal proceedings under section 9 of the 1996 Act 6 must be served on all parties to those proceedings who have given an address for service. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (2) A copy of an application notice under paragraph (1) must be served on any other party to the legal proceedings (whether or not he is within the jurisdiction) who has not given an address for service, at –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (a) his last known address; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (b) a place where it is likely to come to his attention. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (3) Where a question arises as to whether –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (a) an arbitration agreement has been concluded; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] (b) the dispute which is the subject-matter of the proceedings falls within the terms of such an agreement,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.8] the court may decide that question or give directions to enable it to be decided and may order the proceedings to be stayed pending its decision. ## Variation of time

## 62.9

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (1) The court may vary the period of 28 days fixed by section 70(3) of the 1996 Act for –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (a) challenging the award under section 67 or 68 of the Act; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (b) appealing against an award under section 69 of the Act. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (2) An application for an order under paragraph (1) may be made without notice being served on any other party before the period of 28 days expires. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (3) After the period of 28 days has expired –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (a) an application for an order extending time under paragraph (1) must –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (i) be made in the arbitration claim form; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (ii) state the grounds on which the application is made;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (b) any defendant may file written evidence opposing the extension of time within 7 days after service of the arbitration claim form; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.9] (c) if the court extends the period of 28 days, each defendant’s time for acknowledging service and serving evidence shall start to run as if the arbitration claim form had been served on the date when the court’s order is served on that defendant. ## Hearings

## 62.10

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (1) The court may order that an arbitration claim be heard either in public or in private. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (2) Rule 39.2 does not apply. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (3) Subject to any order made under paragraph (1) –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (a) the determination of –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (i) a preliminary point of law under section 45 of the 1996 Act; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (ii) an appeal under section 69 of the 1996 Act on a question of law arising out of an award,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] will be heard in public; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (b) all other arbitration claims will be heard in private. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (4) Paragraph (3)(a) does not apply to –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (a) Omitted

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.10] (b) an application for permission to appeal under section 69(2)(b). ## II OTHER ARBITRATION CLAIMS

## Scope of this Section

## 62.11

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (1) This Section of this Part contains rules about arbitration claims to which the old law applies. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (2) In this Section

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (a) ‘the old law’ means the enactments specified in Schedules 3 and 4 of the 1996 Act as they were in force before their amendment or repeal by that Act; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (b) ‘arbitration claim’ means any application to the court under the old law and includes an appeal (or application for permission to appeal) to the High Court under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act 7 . [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (3) This Section does not apply to –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.11] (a) a claim to which Section III of this Part applies; or (b) a claim on the award. ## Applications to Judge

## 62.12 A claim –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.12 A claim –] (a) seeking permission to appeal under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.12 A claim –] (b) under section 1(5) of that Act (including any claim seeking permission); or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.12 A claim –] (c) under section 5 of that Act,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.12 A claim –] must be made in the High Court and will be heard by a judge of the Commercial Court unless any such judge directs otherwise. ## Starting the claim

## 62.13

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (1) Except where paragraph (2) applies an arbitration claim must be started by the issue of an arbitration claim form in accordance with the Part 8 procedure. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (2) Where an arbitration claim is to be made in existing proceedings –(a) it must be made by way of application notice; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (b) any reference in this Section of this Part to an arbitration claim form includes a reference to an application notice. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (3) The arbitration claim form in an arbitration claim under section 1(5) of the 1979 Act (including any claim seeking permission) must be served on –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (a) the arbitrator or umpire; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.13] (b) any other party to the reference. ## Claims in District Registries

## 62.14

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.14] If –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.14] (a) a claim is to be made under section 12(4) of the 1950 Act 8 for an order for the issue of a witness summons to compel the attendance of the witness before an arbitrator or umpire; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.14] (b) the attendance of the witness is required within the district of a District Registry,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.14] the claim may be started in that Registry. ## Time limits and other special provisions about arbitration claims

## 62.15

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (1) An arbitration claim to

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (a) remit an award under section 22 of the 1950 Act 9 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (b) set aside an award under section 23(2) of that Act 10 or otherwise; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (c) direct an arbitrator or umpire to state the reasons for an award under section 1(5) of the 1979 Act,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] must be made, and the arbitration claim form served, within 21 days after the award has been made and published to the parties. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (2) An arbitration claim to determine any question of law arising in the course of a reference under section 2(1) of the Arbitration Act 1979 must be made, and the arbitration claim form served, within 14 days after –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (a) the arbitrator or umpire gave his consent in writing to the claim being made; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (b) the other parties so consented. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (3) An appeal under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act must be filed, and the arbitration claim form served, within 21 days after the award has been made and published to the parties. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (4) Where reasons material to an appeal under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act are given on a date subsequent to the publication of the award, the period of 21 days referred to in paragraph (3) will run from the date on which reasons are given. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (5) In every arbitration claim to which this rule applies –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (a) the arbitration claim form must state the grounds of the claim or appeal;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (b) where the claim or appeal is based on written evidence, a copy of that evidence must be served with the arbitration claim form; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (c) where the claim or appeal is made with the consent of the arbitrator, the umpire or the other parties, a copy of every written consent must be served with the arbitration claim form. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (6) In an appeal under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (a) a statement of the grounds for the appeal specifying the relevant parts of the award and reasons; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (b) where permission is required, any written evidence in support of the contention that the question of law concerns –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (i) a term of a contract; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (ii) an event,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] which is not a ‘one-off’ term or event,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] must be filed and served with the arbitration claim form. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (7) Any written evidence in reply to written evidence under paragraph (6)(b) must be filed and served on the claimant not less than 2 days before the hearing. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.15] (8) A party to a claim seeking permission to appeal under section 1(2) of the 1979 Act who wishes to contend that the award should be upheld for reasons not expressed or fully expressed in the award and reasons must file and serve on the claimant, a notice specifying the grounds of his contention not less than 2 days before the hearing. ## Service out of the jurisdiction

## 62.16

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (1) Subject to paragraph (2) –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (a) any arbitration claim form in an arbitration claim under the 1950 Act or the 1979 Act; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (b) any order made in such a claim,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] may be served out of the jurisdiction with the permission of the court if the arbitration to which the claim relates –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (i) is governed by the law of England and Wales; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (ii) has been, is being, or will be, held within the jurisdiction. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (2) An arbitration claim form seeking permission to enforce an award may be served out of the jurisdiction with the permission of the court whether or not the arbitration is governed by the law of England and Wales. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (3) An application for permission to serve an arbitration claim form out of the jurisdiction must be supported by written evidence –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (a) stating the grounds on which the application is made; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (b) showing in what place or country the person to be served is, or probably may be found. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] Rules 6.40 to 6.46 apply to the service of an arbitration claim form under paragraph (1). [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (4) Omitted

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.16] (5) An order giving permission to serve an arbitration claim form out of the jurisdiction must specify the period within which the defendant may file an acknowledgment of service. ## III ENFORCEMENT

## Scope of this Section

## 62.17

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.17] This Section of this Part applies to all arbitration enforcement proceedings other than by a claim on the award. ## Enforcement of awards

## 62.18

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (1) An application for permission under –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) section 66 of the 1996 Act 11 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) section 101 of the 1996 Act;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (c) section 26 of the 1950 Act 12 ; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (d) section 3(1)(a) of the 1975 Act 13 ,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] to enforce an award in the same manner as a judgment or order may be made without notice in an arbitration claim form. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (2) The court may specify parties to the arbitration on whom the arbitration claim form must be served. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (3) The parties on whom the arbitration claim form is served must acknowledge service and the enforcement proceedings will continue as if they were an arbitration claim under Section I of this Part. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (4) With the permission of the court the arbitration claim form may be served out of the jurisdiction irrespective of where the award is, or is treated as, made. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (5) Where the applicant applies to enforce an agreed award within the meaning of section 51(2) of the 1996 Act –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) the arbitration claim form must state that the award is an agreed award; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) any order made by the court must also contain such a statement. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (6) An application for permission must be supported by written evidence –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) exhibiting –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (i) where the application is made under section 66 of the 1996 Act or under section 26 of the 1950 Act, the arbitration agreement and the original award (or copies);

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (ii) where the application is under section 101 of the 1996 Act, the documents required to be produced by section 102 of that Act; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (iii) where the application is under section 3(1)(a) of the 1975 Act, the documents required to be produced by section 4 of that Act;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) stating the name and the usual or last known place of residence or business of the claimant and of the person against whom it is sought to enforce the award; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (c) stating either –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (i) that the award has not been complied with; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (ii) the extent to which it has not been complied with at the date of the application. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (7) An order giving permission must –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) be drawn up by the claimant; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) be served on the defendant by –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (i) delivering a copy to him personally; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (ii) sending a copy to him at his usual or last known place of residence or business. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (8) An order giving permission may be served out of the jurisdiction –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) without permission; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) in accordance with rules 6.40 to 6.46 as if the order were an arbitration claim form. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (9) Within 14 days after service of the order or, if the order is to be served out of the jurisdiction, within such other period as the court may set –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) the defendant may apply to set aside the order; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) the award must not be enforced until after –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (i) the end of that period; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (ii) any application made by the defendant within that period has been finally disposed of. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (10) The order must contain a statement of –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (a) the right to make an application to set the order aside; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (b) the restrictions on enforcement under rule 62.18(9)(b). [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.18] (11) Where a body corporate is a party any reference in this rule to place of residence or business shall have effect as if the reference were to the registered or principal address of the body corporate.
